item.title: Maestro 0.8.30
item.description:
## What's new
- **ThunderBridge: the driver now watches the Symphony link itself; Maestro no longer polls the hardware every second.** Driver build 113 follows Apple's model: the OS decides presence, and the driver samples the card's own clock-detect bit (every 2 s while the Symphony is off, every 5 s when idle, never while audio is streaming) and re-locks the link when the clock returns. On the developer's Mac the once-a-second traffic coincided with spontaneous Thunderbolt link drops that clicked the Symphony's relays; the new driver puts no steady-state traffic on the tunnel. - **Wake from sleep re-validates the link.** If the Thunderbolt tunnel was lost during sleep or the card shows a fault, the driver re-runs link initialization and restarts audio. Aimed at the no-audio-after-wake report; not yet confirmed on the reporting system. - Driver change (build 113). The new driver takes over on the next ThunderBridge cable replug or restart.
If you appreciate this work, please consider donating to the [San Francisco Marin Food Bank](https://www.sfmfoodbank.org/).
[Read the full release notes on GitHub](https://github.com/danielraffel/unofficial-symphony-maestro-mk1/releases/tag/v0.8.30)

item.title: Maestro 0.8.29
item.description:
## What's new
- **No more microphone prompt.** 0.8.26 asked for microphone access and claimed macOS 27 required it; that was wrong. Maestro's input meters come from the hardware on both ThunderBridge and USB, so the audio-input entitlement, the usage string, and the input tap are gone. macOS no longer shows the orange microphone indicator or the Mic Mode menu while Maestro is open. If you already allowed it, you can revoke it in System Settings › Privacy & Security › Microphone. - Still open: no audio after wake from sleep on ThunderBridge while everything looks connected. Under investigation; not fixed in this build. - No driver change (build 112).

item.title: Maestro 0.8.28
item.description:
## What's new
- Driver build 112 fixes a kernel panic reported after the ThunderBridge lost power while the Mac was asleep. The driver no longer reads the card's registers while the system is powering down, and on wake it first checks the card is still present before touching it; a unit that lost power now shows as disconnected and comes back on replug instead of panicking the Mac. - Driver change (build 112): macOS asks you to approve the updated driver extension again only if it was not already approved.

item.description:

item.title: Maestro 0.8.22
item.description:
## What's new
- Output Routing now works on ThunderBridge: playback is routed on the ThunderBridge card, as the original Maestro did, so cross-routes such as DAW 1-2 onto Line 3/4 take effect. USB is unchanged. - Saved routes are restored after a Symphony power cycle or cable replug. - Reset Routing on ThunderBridge restores the straight-through table. - Clearing a route (clicking an active cell) no longer crashes Maestro. - Two-card units on ThunderBridge: the second card is fed by playback 17-32, as over USB. - New driver extension (build 111): one ThunderBridge cable unplug/replug after installing.

item.title: Maestro 0.8.21
item.description:
## What's new
- Both USB and Thunderbolt can stay connected: the Symphony's front-panel mode decides which connection Maestro uses, and switching modes is followed automatically in both directions. - Maestro prefers ThunderBridge only when the Symphony actually answers on it, otherwise USB; the status-bar rescan does the same. - While on USB, Maestro keeps watching ThunderBridge and moves back to it as soon as it answers. - Driver extension unchanged (build 110): no cable replug needed for this update.

item.title: Maestro 0.8.20
item.description:
## What's new
- ThunderBridge: a Symphony power cycle now recovers on its own — "Symphony disconnected" within a second when it's off, back to Connected with clean audio a few seconds after it's on, no cable replug or sample-rate change. - ThunderBridge: a Symphony switched on after the driver started is picked up the same way; meters no longer move after the Symphony is powered off; opening Maestro no longer disturbs a running session. - Software Return: pan is back, no 5 dB drop at center, and the meters follow the faders, pan, and mute as on USB. - Clearer status (Disconnected / Symphony disconnected / Connected); the driver banner opens the right System Settings page directly. - USB: on plug-in, Maestro waits for "Symphony I/O : Maestro USB" before choosing an output. - Input, Output, and Mixer remember their scroll position for the session, without the shuffle. - After installing, unplug and replug the ThunderBridge cable once so the new driver extension (build 110) takes over.
